title: Every Patient Can't Tell You What's Wrong
tagline: A full appointment book, a worried owner in the lobby, and a patient who can't tell you where it hurts.

wake_up.text: The clinic opens at eight, but there's already a message on the machine from an anxious owner about their dog not eating since yesterday.

choices.text: Call them back before you even get to the clinic
Wait until you're actually at the clinic to call

clinic_arrival.text: Gloves, scrubs, the smell of antiseptic — the clinic before opening has its own particular quiet.

choices.text: Review today's appointment list

random_moment.text: The morning before opening fills in with the small, unscripted moments of running a clinic — a little different every day.

choices.text: Your vet tech shares a genuinely funny story from yesterday
A supply delivery is running late, complicating the morning
Someone brought real coffee for the whole team today

first_appointment.text: First patient: an elderly cat, routine checkup, owner anxious about every small sound the cat makes.

choices.text: Take the extra time to reassure the owner thoroughly
Keep the appointment efficient — the day is full

morning_appointments.text: The morning moves through vaccinations, a limping dachshund, and a rabbit that absolutely does not want to be examined.

choices.text: Get through the appointment block

lunch_interruption.text: Lunch is interrupted by a front-desk call: a walk-in, a dog that got into something in the yard, vomiting and lethargic.

choices.text: See the walk-in immediately, lunch or not
Finish eating first — the walk-in is stable enough to wait ten minutes

emergency_surgery_prep.text: X-rays show it: a foreign object causing a blockage, and the dog's condition is deteriorating faster than expected.

choices.text: Prep for emergency surgery

surgery_complication.text: Mid-surgery, the dog's vitals suddenly drop — a complication nobody could have predicted from the X-rays, and you have seconds, not minutes, to respond.

choices.text: Stop and stabilize vitals before continuing the procedure
Push through — stopping now is riskier than finishing fast
Call in another vet from down the hall to help manage it
Pause to call the owner before making the call yourself

surgery_outcome_stabilize.text: The extra two minutes stabilizing pays off completely — the rest of the surgery goes clean, and the dog's vitals hold steady the whole way through.

choices.text: Finish the surgery

surgery_outcome_push.text: You finish fast, hands steady despite the dropping numbers. It works — barely — and the recovery afterward is more delicate than it needed to be.

choices.text: Finish the surgery

surgery_outcome_team.text: A second set of hands manages the vitals while you finish the procedure — exactly the kind of moment that makes you grateful for a clinic that isn't a solo operation.

choices.text: Finish the surgery

surgery_outcome_call.text: The call to the owner costs precious minutes during a genuine emergency — informed consent matters, but the timing here nearly cost the patient more than it needed to.

choices.text: Finish the surgery

afternoon_appointments.text: The rest of the afternoon appointment block is waiting, including a nervous new puppy owner with a long list of questions.

choices.text: Answer every question thoroughly, however long it takes
Give the essentials and keep the schedule moving

evening_calls.text: Closing time, but there's still a follow-up call to make to this afternoon's surgery patient's owner.

choices.text: Make the follow-up call yourself before leaving
Let your vet tech handle the follow-up call

end_shift.text: The clinic goes quiet for the night. Somewhere across town, a dog that almost didn't make it is resting comfortably.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: The Save of the Week
triumphant.blurb: Every call today held, including the one that mattered most. This is the day clients tell their friends about.

steady_hand.title: Solid Day
steady_hand.blurb: No headlines, no hesitation — just careful, competent care for every patient, all day long.

ordinary_day.title: Full Appointment Book
ordinary_day.blurb: A busy, ordinary day treating a full slate of patients. Tomorrow's book is just as full.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it to closing, but you're not sure how. This pace, patient after patient, has a real cost.

written_up.title: Case Review
written_up.blurb: A few of today's calls are heading into a formal case review. The patients are safe. The clinic still wants to understand the decisions.
